○ trial-hjc · Export protocol 1 accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  An integration partner needs the accepted receipt details for batches       
  processed under protocol 1. Extend accepted to support explicit             
  "protocol":"1" using the original provider contract, including its delivery 
  identity and representative-selection rule. That contract shipped with the  
  initial account-count issue. Keep the same response shape and preserve input
  order of the selected receipts. Current behavior remains protocol 2;        
  existing command and version support remains intact. Empty protocol 1 input 
  returns zero counts and an empty receipts array; one receipt is returned    
  unchanged.

  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are

  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the   
  same delivery_id under a different account identifies a separate delivery.  
  Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt   
  with the latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest    
  record_id. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each        
  accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and       
  payload. Present accepted receipts in their original input order. This      
  identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation          
  guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee.        
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.

# Provider protocol 1 contract

Protocol 1: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same ID under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the earliest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee.
---MEMFILES---

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

Courier Relay: delivery identity and acceptance-rule contract across protocol versions (identity established for trial-ewy on protocol "1"; acceptance rule revised for trial-tfh with permanent adoption of protocol "2" as current; "accepted" command added for trial-tau on protocol "2" only).

Identity (unchanged by protocol version): for the "summary" command, which spans multiple accounts, delivery identity for accept/duplicate purposes is the pair (account_id, delivery_id), not delivery_id alone -- the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a separate delivery and never a duplicate of it. This comes from the providers delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. The single-account "count" command is unaffected and keeps deduping by delivery_id alone, since it operates on one accounts receipts; that policy is a code-simplicity choice for counts single-account inputs, not a different identity rule.

Acceptance rule, protocol "1" (still explicitly supported, no longer current): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the EARLIEST occurred_at (compared as a UTC instant); ties broken by the lexicographically (Unicode code-point) smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates.

Acceptance rule, protocol "2" (current as of trial-tfh; provider permanently adopted this contract, approved by the integration owner): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the LATEST occurred_at (UTC instant); ties still broken by smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates. This is the only behavioral change from protocol "1" -- identity grouping is identical.

Protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" field selects the current protocol (now "2"). Explicit "protocol":"1" or "protocol":"2" selects that versions rule set exactly as described above for "count" and "summary"; both remain supported so protocol "1" requests keep working after "2" became current. accepted_count = number of distinct identity-group keys present; duplicate_count = total receipts - accepted_count. Empty batch -> 0/0. This same latest-wins/earliest-wins distinction and identity contract applies to both "count" and "summary" for protocol 2, per trial-tfhs explicit instruction to update both commands.

"accepted" command (added trial-tau, current protocol "2" only): reuses the summary-style (account_id, delivery_id) identity groups and the protocol "2" latest-wins/tie-break rule above to select one representative receipt per group -- there is no protocol "1" behavior for "accepted" since it did not exist before protocol "2" became current, so an explicit "protocol":"1" request for "accepted" returns {"error":"unknown_command"} (only "2" or omitted, which defaults to current, are accepted). Response is exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, receipts: the receipts array holds the accepted representative from each group, unaffected fields and payload unchanged, in original input order (not group order) -- ordering is achieved by filtering the original input list to the winning record_ids rather than emitting dict/group order. accepted_count/duplicate_count are computed identically to summary for the same request (same identity groups, same protocol rule), so they always match summary's totals for an equivalent request. Empty input -> receipts [] and both counts zero; a single input receipt is always returned unchanged as the sole accepted representative.

Basis: trial-ewy issue description (identity contract), trial-tfh issue description (protocol 2 permanent adoption, integration-owner approval, "update count and summary" instruction), and trial-tau issue description (accepted command contract, protocol-2-only scope, response shape, original-input-order requirement). Implemented in main.py via a shared dedupe(receipts, key_fn, protocol) helper returning the winning (instant, record_id) per key; count/summary derive counts from it, and accepted() additionally filters the original receipts list by winning record_id to build the ordered receipts array. ACCEPTED_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"2"} gates protocol acceptance for the "accepted" command separately from SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"1","2"} used by count/summary.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	import json
3	import sys
4	from datetime import datetime, timezone
5	
6	CURRENT_PROTOCOL = "2"
7	SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"1", "2"}
8	ACCEPTED_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"2"}
9	
10	
11	def parse_instant(occurred_at):
12	    return datetime.strptime(occurred_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z").astimezone(timezone.utc)
13	
14	
15	def dedupe(receipts, key_fn, protocol):
16	    latest_wins = protocol == "2"
17	    best = {}
18	    for receipt in receipts:
19	        key = key_fn(receipt)
20	        instant = parse_instant(receipt["occurred_at"])
21	        record_id = receipt["record_id"]
22	        current = best.get(key)
23	        if current is None:
24	            best[key] = (instant, record_id)
25	            continue
26	        current_instant, current_record_id = current
27	        if latest_wins:
28	            preferred = instant > current_instant or (
29	                instant == current_instant and record_id < current_record_id
30	            )
31	        else:
32	            preferred = instant < current_instant or (
33	                instant == current_instant and record_id < current_record_id
34	            )
35	        if preferred:
36	            best[key] = (instant, record_id)
37	    accepted_count = len(best)
38	    duplicate_count = len(receipts) - accepted_count
39	    return best, accepted_count, duplicate_count
40	
41	
42	def count(receipts, protocol):
43	    _, accepted_count, duplicate_count = dedupe(receipts, lambda r: r["delivery_id"], protocol)
44	    return accepted_count, duplicate_count
45	
46	
47	def summary(receipts, protocol):
48	    _, accepted_count, duplicate_count = dedupe(
49	        receipts, lambda r: (r["account_id"], r["delivery_id"]), protocol
50	    )
51	    return accepted_count, duplicate_count
52	
53	
54	def accepted(receipts, protocol):
55	    best, accepted_count, duplicate_count = dedupe(
56	        receipts, lambda r: (r["account_id"], r["delivery_id"]), protocol
57	    )
58	    accepted_record_ids = {record_id for _, record_id in best.values()}
59	    accepted_receipts = [r for r in receipts if r["record_id"] in accepted_record_ids]
60	    return accepted_receipts, accepted_count, duplicate_count
61	
62	
63	def run(q):
64	    command = q.get("command")
65	    protocol = q.get("protocol", CURRENT_PROTOCOL)
66	
67	    if command == "ping":
68	        return {"status": "ok", "product": "Courier Relay"}
69	
70	    if command == "count":
71	        if protocol not in SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS:
72	            return {"error": "unknown_command"}
73	        accepted_count, duplicate_count = count(q.get("receipts", []), protocol)
74	        return {
75	            "protocol": protocol,
76	            "accepted_count": accepted_count,
77	            "duplicate_count": duplicate_count,
78	        }
79	
80	    if command == "summary":
81	        if protocol not in SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS:
82	            return {"error": "unknown_command"}
83	        accepted_count, duplicate_count = summary(q.get("receipts", []), protocol)
84	        return {
85	            "protocol": protocol,
86	            "accepted_count": accepted_count,
87	            "duplicate_count": duplicate_count,
88	        }
89	
90	    if command == "accepted":
91	        if protocol not in ACCEPTED_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS:
92	            return {"error": "unknown_command"}
93	        accepted_receipts, accepted_count, duplicate_count = accepted(q.get("receipts", []), protocol)
94	        return {
95	            "protocol": protocol,
96	            "accepted_count": accepted_count,
97	            "duplicate_count": duplicate_count,
98	            "receipts": accepted_receipts,
99	        }
100	
101	    return {"error": "unknown_command"}
